Toën (2020, Theorem 0.1) treats simply connected spaces of finite type: integral affinization has homotopy sheaves $\pi_i(X)\otimes\mathbb H$, where $\mathbb H$ is the Hilbert additive group, and the map to its integral points has a functorial retraction. In a divided-power algebra, \(T^{[r]}T^{[s]}=\binom{r+s}{r}T^{[r+s]}\), so the separate additive identifications \(\mathbb ZT^{[w]}\cong\mathbb Z\) cannot all be multiplicative. If the canonical derived comparison respects products, classes represented in weights \(r,s\) multiply to the ordinary cup product times this binomial coefficient, not automatically to the same unweighted class. This elementary test is a concrete way to qualify the planning statement without denying the information carried by the weighted model.

For \(BC_2\) over \(\mathbb F_2\), the normalized group cochains have one generator in every degree, zero differential, and the cup powers of the degree-one generator are nonzero, giving \(H^*(BC_2;\mathbb F_2)=\mathbb F_2[t]\), equivalently the projective-space calculation in Hatcher (2002, online version, Theorem 3.19). An alternating differential graded algebra has square zero on odd-degree elements, so it cannot have this graded cohomology ring through a product-preserving identification. This rules out that strengthened unweighted interpretation, while a weighted construction with its binomial coefficient product avoids the asserted identification and is not contradicted by the test.

Over \(\mathbb F_2\), the central binomial coefficient \(\binom{2w}{w}\) is even for \(w>0\), so the square of an odd class represented in a single weight can vanish consistently with alternation. Yet the degree-one class of \(BC_2\) represented once in weight one and once in weight two has product coefficient \(\binom31=3=1\) in \(\mathbb F_2\), giving its nonzero ordinary square in weight three under the comparison. Consequently the test in R050 rejects identifying all these representatives with one unweighted algebra element; it does not show that the weighted system loses every nonzero cup product.

Let \(X=\Delta^1/\partial\Delta^1\), let \(k\) be a field, and define a presheaf \(F\) on \(\Delta/X\) by \(F(\sigma)=k\) on simplices degenerate from the unique vertex and \(F(\sigma)=0\) on simplices degenerate from the nondegenerate edge, with identity and zero restriction maps as appropriate. Every section of \(C_X^q\otimes_kF\) is zero: the edge forces its vertex value to vanish, and maps from vertex-degenerate simplices to that vertex force all remaining values to vanish. In contrast, embed \(F\) diagonally into the injective presheaf \(I\) right-adjoint to vertex evaluation, for which \(I(\sigma)=k^{\dim\sigma+1}\); then \(\Gamma I=k\), \(\Gamma(I/F)=k^2\), and the map between them is diagonal, so the long exact sequence gives \(H^1(X,F)\cong k\). Thus the pointwise exact tensor resolution does not compute derived sections for this arbitrary coefficient sheaf, and its terms cannot all have the claimed acyclicity; the full category/variance verification is recorded in `research/algebra_checks.md`.

Ekedahl (2002, Theorem 2.9 and Lemma 2.8) models connected nilpotent spaces with finitely generated homology in each degree using numerical maps, namely rational polynomials taking integral values on integral inputs. Numerical cochains recover cohomology and the mapping comparison between these special models is up to numerical homotopy (based maps in Lemma 2.8), while minimal models need not be strictly isomorphic. This offers a precise later alternative to ordinary integral polynomial maps, not an identification with the completed PD dual on these scans.

Horel (2024, Theorems 5.4 and 6.1) obtains a fully faithful model for connected nilpotent finite-type spaces using cosimplicial binomial rings localized at quasi-isomorphisms; for connected finite-type spaces more generally the derived unit is integral Bousfield–Kan completion. The binomial condition and its derived category are not interchangeable with a PD ideal, so this result supplies a modern comparison target without completing the manuscript’s uniqueness argument.
